The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America
17M.3 Avenge not yourselves, for vengeance is in God's hands.

precepts.text: Fear not, O my servant Jacob, be not dismayed, O Israel: for behold, I will save thee from afar off. It is Israel who is afar off.
precepts.point: But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. Who was afar off? Israel. These Ephesians in Ephesus are Israelites scattered in Ephesus. He is our peace: not everybody's peace. Christ is the peace that brings both nations, the southern and northern kingdom, back together.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:13: “But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who was afar off? We deal with precepts. These Christians like to say, let's go to the Greek, let's go to this book, let's go to that. We stick to the scriptures and stay within our book.

“But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off.” It is Israel who is afar off.

It's really that simple. The ones who were far off and are made nigh by the blood of Christ are Israel. Then verse 14: “For he is our peace.” Our peace, not everybody's peace. Reading from verse 12 down to verse 14, the our becomes plain: these Ephesians in Ephesus are Israelites scattered in Ephesus.

precepts.text: Fear not, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel, for I will save thee from afar off and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.point: Jeremiah 46:27: fear not, O my servant Jacob, because Jacob's trouble and Armageddon are coming; I will save thee from afar off, this far-off land, and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:17 ends, “they shall behold the land that is very far off”, and that land is Jerusalem. Jeremiah shows how we get back to it.

“But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel”. He says it because of great tribulation: Jacob's trouble will be coming. Tribulation leads into Armageddon. World War III has already begun, and in the middle of that will be Armageddon. So the Lord says, fear not, be not dismayed.

“for, behold, I will save thee from afar off”, because we have been taken captive into far off lands; here in America is a far off land. “and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease”. We ain't going to be bothered by anybody; we shall be in rest and at ease. “and none shall make him afraid”: there is no nation that is going to make us afraid ever, ever again.

So the one whose eyes see the King in his beauty is also brought out of the far off land of his captivity to behold the land that is very far off, Jerusalem, and dwell there in rest.

precepts.text: Let us go again to our own people, from the oppressing sword.
precepts.point: The Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and setteth up over it the basest of men. God allows what Trump is doing.
precepts.why:
“He made many to fall, yea, one fell upon another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword.” The oppressing sword is the wicked, the sword of Psalms 17:13. And an oppressing sword is being risen up all over the earth, especially on the western hemisphere, and especially amongst our people.

Everything you see taking place with ICE, with how America went into Venezuela and snatched up its president, Trump telling the leader in Colombia he is next: that is the oppressing sword. We are living in the beginning of sorrows. It is going to get worse and worse, beyond the worst things you could think of. You thought World War II was bad; wait till you see what is about to happen on this earth. Don't sit back and be comfortable because nothing has happened to you yet.

God is using America, that administration, as his sword to bring judgment on the earth. It is the wine cup of Jeremiah 25:15: “Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.” And Jeremiah 51:7 shows whose hand that cup is in: “Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.” Babylon is not just ancient Babylon; it is America. What is in that cup is falsehood, lies, oppression and ill dealing, and that is why the nations are becoming angry with America.

So under that oppressing sword, many fall, and the cry goes up: “let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity”. This is why Daniel 4:17 matters now: the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, he has raised up the wicked as his sword over this side of the world where Israel is, and he is using it to bring judgment on the earth.

points: The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah against the gentiles, against Egypt and the army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim.
The Egyptians are gentiles and heathens; they are called to order the buckler and shield, draw near to battle, harness the horses, furnish the spears, and put on the brigandines.

Yet the Most High has seen them dismayed and turned back, their mighty ones beaten down and fleeing without looking back, for fear was round about; the swift shall not flee away nor the mighty man escape, stumbling and falling toward the north by the river Euphrates.

Egypt rises up like a flood whose waters are moved like the rivers, boasting he will go up and cover the earth and destroy the city and its inhabitants, calling forth his horses, chariots, and mighty men, the Ethiopians, Libyans, and Lydians that handle the shield and bend the bow.

But this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance to avenge Him of His adversaries; the sword shall devour and be made drunk with their blood, for the Most High has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.

The virgin daughter of Egypt is told to go up into Gilead and take balm, but in vain shall she use many medicines, for she shall not be cured; the nations have heard of her shame and her cry filled the land as her mighty men stumbled and fell together.

The Most High spoke to Jeremiah how Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt; the word is to be declared in Migdol, Noph, and Tahpanhes, calling them to stand fast and prepare, for the sword shall devour round about them.

Their valiant men are swept away and stand not because the Most High drove them; they fall one upon another and say let us go again to our own people and the land of our nativity from the oppressing sword.

Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise who has passed the time appointed; as surely as Tabor is among the mountains and Carmel by the sea, so shall the conqueror come, and the daughter dwelling in Egypt must furnish herself to go into captivity, for Noph shall be waste and desolate without inhabitant.

Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction comes out of the north; even her hired men in the midst of her are like fatted bullocks, turned back and fled away together, not standing because the day of their calamity and the time of their visitation was upon them.

The voice shall go like a serpent as they march with an army and come against her with axes like hewers of wood to cut down her forest, though it cannot be searched, because they are more than the grasshoppers and are innumerable.

The Most High will punish the multitude of No, Pharaoh, and Egypt with their gods and their kings, delivering them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and his servants; afterward it shall be inhabited as in the days of old.

The Most High turns to comfort His own, telling Jacob His servant not to fear nor be dismayed, for He will save him from afar off and his seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease with none to make him afraid.

He will make a full end of all the nations where He has driven us, but He will not make a full end of us; He will correct us in measure and will not leave us wholly unpunished, so there is redemption for us but still a reminder of punishment because of our sins.
